questions.topic: Pointers and Strings — Difference Between sizeof(s) and strlen(s)
questions.q: What will `printf("%zu %zu", sizeof(s), strlen(s))` output for pointer `char *s = "Hello"` on a 64-bit system?
questions.hint: Does sizeof evaluate the size of a pointer variable or the size of a string literal?
explanations: Correct! Variable `s` has pointer type (`char*`), so `sizeof(s)` on a 64-bit system is 8 bytes. Function `strlen(s)` counts the number of characters up to the null terminator, which is 5. Output: `8 5`.
Incorrect. 6 would be the size of array `char[6]` if the declaration were `char s[] = "Hello"`.
Incorrect. `sizeof` of a pointer does not depend on the length of the string it points to.
Incorrect. `strlen` does not include the trailing null terminator `'\0'` in the string length.

questions.topic: Pointer Arithmetic — Pointer to Entire Array &a and Past-the-End Shift
questions.q: What is expression `*(ptr - 1)` equal to if `ptr` is created as `(int*)(&a + 1)` for array `int a[5] = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}`?
questions.hint: How many bytes does expression `&a + 1` shift the address?
explanations: Correct! `&a` has type 'pointer to array of 5 elements' (`int(*)[5]`). The shift `&a + 1` shifts the pointer immediately by the size of the ENTIRE array ($5 \times 4 = 20$ bytes), pointing to the area right past the last element. Casting to `int*` and taking a subsequent step backward `ptr - 1` returns a pointer to element `a[4]`, which equals 5.
Incorrect. 1 is the first element `a[0]`.
Incorrect. The pointer goes out of array bounds before subtracting 1, but `ptr - 1` points back to valid element `a[4]`, so there is no UB.
Incorrect. Type casting is syntactically correct in C.

questions.topic: Operator Precedence — Postfix Pointer Increment *p++
questions.q: What will `printf("%d", *p++)` output for `int a[3] = {10, 20, 30}` and `int *p = a`?
questions.hint: What value does postfix increment `p++` return — old or new?
explanations: Correct! Postfix `++` has higher precedence than dereference `*`, but returns the OLD value of pointer `p`. The original address `&a[0]` (value 10) is dereferenced, after which `p` increments and points to `a[1]`.
Incorrect. 20 would be printed with prefix increment `*++p`.
Incorrect. 11 would be obtained when dereferencing with value increment `(*p)++`.
Incorrect. Array element values do not change with `*p++`.

questions.topic: Operator Precedence — Prefix Pointer Increment *++p
questions.q: What will `printf("%d", *++p)` output for `int a[3] = {10, 20, 30}` and `int *p = a`?
questions.hint: When exactly does the pointer shift happen with prefix increment?
explanations: Correct! Prefix `++` first shifts pointer `p` to the next element (`a[1]`), and then operator `*` dereferences the resulting address. The value of `a[1]` is 20.
Incorrect. 10 is the value of `a[0]`, dereferenced before increment.
Incorrect. 11 would be obtained by incrementing the value itself `++*p`.
Incorrect. 30 is the third element `a[2]`.

questions.topic: Function Parameters — Array Decay to Pointer in Function Parameters
questions.q: What will `sizeof(arr)` output inside function `void func(int arr[100])` on a 64-bit system?
questions.hint: Does function parameter `int arr[100]` preserve its fixed size when passed?
explanations: Correct! In function parameters, array declaration `int arr[100]` is automatically converted by compiler syntax to pointer `int *arr`. Pointer size on a 64-bit platform is 8 bytes.
Incorrect. 400 bytes ($100 \times 4$) would be returned by `sizeof` if the array were in the same local context, not in function parameters.
Incorrect. 100 is element count, not size in bytes.
Incorrect. 4 bytes is the size of a single `int` element.

questions.topic: Structures — Assigning Structures with Embedded Arrays
questions.q: What is element `d2.arr[1]` equal to after executing `d2 = d1` for a structure with an embedded array?
questions.hint: Are array elements copied when assigning structures to each other?
explanations: Correct! Arrays in C cannot be assigned directly, but when assigning structures (`d2 = d1`), the byte-for-byte copy (memberwise copy) fully copies the contents of the embedded array. Element `d2.arr[1]` equals 2.
Incorrect. 1 is element `d2.arr[0]`.
Incorrect. 3 is element `d2.arr[2]`.
Incorrect. Structure assignment is permitted by the C standard.

questions.topic: sizeof Operator — Absence of Side Effects Evaluation
questions.q: What will variable `i` equal after executing the line `sizeof(a[i++])`?
questions.hint: Is the expression inside sizeof operator evaluated during runtime?
explanations: Correct! The `sizeof` operator is evaluated at compile time (for fixed-size types) and does NOT evaluate its expression at runtime. Expression `i++` inside `sizeof` is not executed, so `i` remains 0.
Incorrect. 1 would occur if the `sizeof` operand were executed at runtime.
Incorrect. Absence of side effects evaluation in `sizeof` is guaranteed by the C standard.
Incorrect. Expression syntax inside `sizeof` is completely correct.

questions.topic: Memory — Initialization of Static Arrays static
questions.q: What is element `a[0]` equal to for an uninitialized static array `static int a[3]`?
questions.hint: What replaces memory garbage for variables with static storage duration (static)?
explanations: Correct! Variables and arrays with static storage duration (`static` or global) are automatically initialized to zero by the C standard (`BSS` segment) if no explicit values are provided. `a[0]` is guaranteed to equal 0.
Incorrect. Indeterminate memory garbage is characteristic only of local automatic (`auto`) variables.
Incorrect. Reading a statically zeroed element is completely safe.
Incorrect. Declaring static arrays without initialization is allowed.

questions.topic: 2D Arrays — Dereferencing Syntax *(*(a + i) + j)
questions.q: What is expression `*(*(a + 1) + 1)` equal to for `int a[2][3] = {{10, 20, 30}, {40, 50, 60}}`?
questions.hint: Which matrix element `a[i][j]` does this notation correspond to?
explanations: Correct! Expression `*(*(a + i) + j)` is fully equivalent to `a[i][j]`. For `i = 1` and `j = 1` we request element `a[1][1]`, which equals 50.
Incorrect. 20 is element `a[0][1]` (`*(*(a + 0) + 1)`).
Incorrect. 40 is element `a[1][0]` (`*(*(a + 1) + 0)`).
Incorrect. 60 is element `a[1][2]` (`*(*(a + 1) + 2)`).

questions.topic: String Arrays — Fixed Size char a[3] Without Null Terminator
questions.q: What is `sizeof(a)` equal to for declaration `char a[3] = "ABC"`?
questions.hint: Does the null terminator fit into a 3-byte array when initialized with three characters?
explanations: Correct! Under C89/C99 standards, it is allowed to initialize a fixed-length character array with a string literal of the exact same length. The null terminator `'\0'` is discarded, and the array contains exactly 3 elements. `sizeof(a)` is 3.
Incorrect. 4 bytes would be the size of `a` if it were declared as `char a[] = "ABC"` (including `'\0'`).
Incorrect. 8 is the size of pointer `char*`.
Incorrect. C compiler permits this construct without error (unlike C++).

questions.topic: Pointers — Negative Subscripting After Pointer Shift
questions.q: What is value `p[-1]` equal to if `p += 3` was executed after `p = a` for `int a[4] = {1, 2, 3, 4}`?
questions.hint: Which element does `p` point to after `p += 3` and where does `p[-1]` access?
explanations: Correct! `p += 3` shifts pointer to element `a[3]` (value 4). Subscript `p[-1]` is equivalent to `*(p - 1)`, moving one element backward — to `a[2]`, equal to 3.
Incorrect. 4 is current element `p[0]` (`a[3]`).
Incorrect. 2 is element `p[-2]` (`a[1]`).
Incorrect. 1 is element `p[-3]` (`a[0]`).

questions.topic: Double Pointers — Distinction and Double Dereference **pp
questions.q: What will `printf("%d", **pp)` output for `int a = 5`, `int *p = &a` and `int **pp = &p`?
questions.hint: How many times must a pointer to pointer `int**` be dereferenced to reach the value of variable `a`?
explanations: Correct! `pp` points to `p`. First dereference `*pp` gives the value of `p` (address `&a`). Second dereference `**pp` retrieves the value of variable `a` itself, which is 5.
Incorrect. Address of variable `a` would be obtained with single dereference `*pp`.
Incorrect. Address of pointer `p` is the value of `pp` itself without dereference signs.
Incorrect. Double pointer with double dereferencing is standard syntax.

questions.topic: Memory — Contiguous Access to 2D Array via Single Pointer p + 3
questions.q: What is expression `*(p + 3)` equal to for `int a[2][2] = {{1, 2}, {3, 4}}` and `int *p = &a[0][0]`?
questions.hint: In what order are 2D array elements stored in memory?
explanations: Correct! In C, array elements are stored sequentially: `a[0][0]` (1), `a[0][1]` (2), `a[1][0]` (3), `a[1][1]` (4). Pointer `p + 3` points to 4th element of this memory block (`a[1][1]`), equal to 4.
Incorrect. 3 is element `a[1][0]` (`*(p + 2)`).
Incorrect. 2 is element `a[0][1]` (`*(p + 1)`).
Incorrect. 1 is initial element `a[0][0]` (`*p`).

questions.topic: Pointer Arithmetic — Zero Difference of Same Addresses p - a
questions.q: What is difference `p - a` equal to if pointer `p` is initialized as `char *p = a` for string `char a[] = "Hello"`?
questions.hint: Do `p` and `a` point to the same or different addresses immediately after initialization?
explanations: Correct! Variable `p` points to the same address where array `a` begins (`&a[0]`). Subtracting two pointers referencing the exact same memory cell returns 0.
Incorrect. 5 is length of string `Hello`, but pointer subtraction shows offset between addresses, not length.
Incorrect. 6 is total array size `char a[6]`.
Incorrect. Subtracting pointers of the same type is correct.

questions.topic: Syntax — Swapping Index and Array: 2[a]
questions.q: What is expression `2[a]` equal to for array `int a[3] = {10, 20, 30}`?
questions.hint: How is subscript operator `x[y]` expanded via pointers?
explanations: Correct! Expression `a[i]` under C standard turns into `*(a + i)`. Thanks to commutativity of addition, `*(a + i)` is equivalent to `*(i + a)`, which can be written as `i[a]`. Writing `2[a]` is exactly equal to `a[2]`, which is 30.
Incorrect. 10 is `0[a]` (or `a[0]`).
Incorrect. 20 is `1[a]` (or `a[1]`).
Incorrect. Swapping index and array name is valid C syntax.

questions.topic: Pointers — Positive Index Relative to Shifted Pointer p[2]
questions.q: What is result of expression `p[2]` equal to if `p = a + 1` for array `int a[] = {10, 20, 30, 40}`?
questions.hint: Which index of original array `a` is requested when calling `p[2]`?
explanations: Correct! Pointer `p` references `a[1]` (value 20). Writing `p[2]` transforms into `*(p + 2)`, shifting another 2 elements right and reading `a[3]`, equal to 40.
Incorrect. 30 is element `p[1]` (`a[2]`).
Incorrect. 20 is element `p[0]` (`a[1]`).
Incorrect. 10 is element `p[-1]` (`a[0]`).

questions.topic: Constness — Constant Pointer int * const p
questions.q: What will happen when evaluating code with constant pointer `int * const p = &a` and modifying `*p = 30`?
questions.hint: Does syntax `int * const p` forbid modifying data at address pointed to by `p`?
explanations: Correct! Writing `int * const p` declares a CONSTANT POINTER (cannot change address `p` itself), but data `*p` can be changed. Command `*p = 30` successfully overwrites variable `a` value to 30.
Incorrect. Error would occur when attempting to change address itself, e.g., `p = &b`.
Incorrect. Value of `a` successfully changed via dereference.
Incorrect. Code fully complies with C language specification.

questions.topic: Characters and Types — Pointer Arithmetic with sizeof Results
questions.q: Which character will `printf` output given 4-byte `int` for `char a[] = "123456"`?
questions.hint: What is difference `sizeof(int) - 1` equal to and which character lies at this index?
explanations: Correct! With `sizeof(int) == 4`, offset will be $4 - 1 = 3$. Expression `*(a + 3)` is equivalent to `a[3]`. String indexing starts from zero: `a[0]='1'`, `a[1]='2'`, `a[2]='3'`, `a[3]='4'`. Character `'4'` is output.
Incorrect. Character `'3'` is at index `a[2]`.
Incorrect. Character `'5'` is at index `a[4]`.
Incorrect. Character `'2'` is at index `a[1]`.

questions.topic: Strings — Modifying Character Array char a[]
questions.q: What will `printf` output after modifying `a[0] = 'b'` for array `char a[] = "cat"`?
questions.hint: Is a string copy created when initializing local array `char a[]`?
explanations: Correct! Declaring `char a[] = "cat"` allocates a local array on stack and copies string literal characters there. This array is mutable. Changing `a[0] = 'b'` turns the word into `"bat"`.
Incorrect. Character `a[0]` was successfully overwritten.
Incorrect. Memory access error would occur when declaring a pointer to constant literal `char *a = "cat"`.
Incorrect. Modifying local character array is permitted.

questions.topic: 2D Arrays — Indexing in Partial Initialization
questions.q: What is element `a[1][1]` equal to for matrix `int a[3][2] = {1, 2, 3}`?
questions.hint: How are initializers laid out across matrix rows `[3][2]`?
explanations: Correct! Matrix has 3 rows of 2 elements. Values are distributed in order: `a[0][0]=1`, `a[0][1]=2`, `a[1][0]=3`. All remaining elements (`a[1][1]`, `a[2][0]`, `a[2][1]`) are filled with zeros. `a[1][1]` equals 0.
Incorrect. 3 is element `a[1][0]`.
Incorrect. 2 is element `a[0][1]`.
Incorrect. 1 is element `a[0][0]`.

questions.topic: Operators — Preserving Value in Postfix Increment *p++
questions.q: What will `printf` output for variables `x` and `*p` after evaluating `int x = *p++`?
questions.hint: What value is returned into `x` and which element does `p` move to?
explanations: Correct! Postfix increment returns initial address `p` (`&a[0]`), dereferencing which writes 5 into variable `x`. After that `p` shifts to next element `a[1]` (value 10). Output: `5 10`.
Incorrect. Second number is 10, since `p` advanced to second element.
Incorrect. `x` receives old value 5, not new.
Incorrect. Third element 15 is untouched.

questions.topic: Arrays of Pointers — Double Subscripting arr[1][2]
questions.q: Which character will `printf` output for double subscripting `arr[1][2]` for `char *arr[] = {"apple", "banana", "cherry"}`?
questions.hint: Select string by first index and character by second index.
explanations: Correct! `arr[1]` selects second string `"banana"`. Subscript `[2]` requests 3rd character of this string (`'b'` - 0, `'a'` - 1, `'n'` - 2). Character `'n'` is printed.
Incorrect. `'a'` is at indices `arr[1][1]` or `arr[1][3]`.
Incorrect. `'b'` is first character `arr[1][0]`.
Incorrect. `'p'` is in first string `arr[0][1]`.

questions.topic: 2D Arrays — Shifting Row Pointer **(p + 2)
questions.q: What is expression `**(p + 2)` equal to for row pointer `int (*p)[3] = a` of matrix `int a[3][3]`?
questions.hint: Which row does pointer shift `p + 2` move to and which element is returned upon dereference?
explanations: Correct! `p + 2` shifts pointer to 3rd row subarray `{7, 8, 9}`. First dereference `*(p + 2)` gives array of 3rd row, and second `**(p + 2)` retrieves its first element `a[2][0]`, equal to 7.
Incorrect. 1 is element `**p` (`a[0][0]`).
Incorrect. 4 is element `**(p + 1)` (`a[1][0]`).
Incorrect. 9 is element `a[2][2]`.

questions.topic: sizeof Operator — char Array Without String Literal
questions.q: What is `sizeof(a)` equal to for explicit list initialization `char a[] = {'a', 'b', 'c'}`?
questions.hint: Does the compiler add a null terminator when initializing arrays via character constants in curly braces?
explanations: Correct! Automatic null terminator `'\0'` is added by compiler ONLY when initializing with string literal `"abc"`. When initializing with character list `{...}`, array contains exactly specified 3 elements. `sizeof` is 3.
Incorrect. 4 bytes would be output for string literal `"abc"`.
Incorrect. 8 is size of pointer `char*`.
Incorrect. List initialization of array elements is completely correct.

questions.topic: Pointer Arithmetic — Address Difference &a[2] - &a[0]
questions.q: What is difference `&a[2] - &a[0]` equal to for array `int a[3] = {10, 25, 40}`?
questions.hint: Calculate index difference between two slots.
explanations: Correct! Difference of pointers to elements of same array calculates element count between them: $2 - 0 = 2$.
Incorrect. 8 bytes would be obtained when explicitly casting pointers to byte type `char*`.
Incorrect. 30 would be obtained when subtracting element values `a[2] - a[0]` ($40 - 10 = 30$), but code subtracts their addresses `&`.
Incorrect. 3 is total element count in array.

questions.topic: Bitwise Operations — Bitwise AND (&) with Dereferenced Value
questions.q: What will `printf` output when executing bitwise AND `*p & b` for `a = 4` and `b = 2`?
questions.hint: Convert numbers 4 and 2 to binary system and perform AND operation.
explanations: Correct! `*p` equals 4 (`100` in binary), `b` equals 2 (`010` in binary). Bitwise AND operation (`100 & 010`) returns `000`, which is 0.
Incorrect. 6 is obtained with bitwise OR (`4 | 2`).
Incorrect. 2 would be obtained if set bits matched.
Incorrect. 4 is initial value `*p`.

questions.topic: Macros and Size — Classic Pattern sizeof(a) / sizeof(a[0])
questions.q: What is expression `sizeof(a) / sizeof(a[0])` equal to for array `int a[] = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}`?
questions.hint: Which property of array does this formula calculate?
explanations: Correct! This is a standard C idiom to determine array element count. Total array size in bytes (24) is divided by single element size (4): $24 / 4 = 6$.
Incorrect. 24 is full array size in bytes `sizeof(a)`.
Incorrect. 4 is size of single `int` element in bytes.
Incorrect. Result does not depend on specific values inside array.

questions.topic: Passing Parameters — Passing Pointer by Value to Function
questions.q: What will `printf("%d", *p)` output after calling function `step(p)` that modifies local pointer?
questions.hint: Will pointer `p` itself in calling function main change after increment inside `step`?
explanations: Correct! Pointers in C are passed to functions BY VALUE (a local copy of address is created). Function `step` shifts its copy of pointer, while original pointer `p` in `main` continues pointing to `a[0]`, equal to 10.
Incorrect. 20 would be output if parameter were passed as pointer to pointer `int **p`.
Incorrect. Array element values are not zeroed.
Incorrect. Code for calling and passing pointer is correct.

questions.topic: Memory — Flat Shift Relative to &a[0][0] by + 4
questions.q: What is expression `*(&a[0][0] + 4)` equal to for matrix `int a[2][3] = {10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60}`?
questions.hint: Count 4 elements in continuous matrix memory sequence.
explanations: Correct! Array is located continuously: 0:10, 1:20, 2:30, 3:40, 4:50, 5:60. Shift of 4 elements relative to first slot leads to value 50 (`a[1][1]`).
Incorrect. 40 is element with shift +3 (`a[1][0]`).
Incorrect. 60 is element with shift +5 (`a[1][2]`).
Incorrect. 30 is element with shift +2 (`a[0][2]`).

questions.topic: Arithmetic — Calculating Offset Index via Element Difference *(a + offset)
questions.q: What is expression `*(a + (a[2] - a[0]))` equal to for array `int a[3] = {1, 2, 3}`?
questions.hint: First calculate element value difference `a[2] - a[0]`, then apply shift.
explanations: Correct! Calculate value inside parentheses: `a[2] - a[0]` $= 3 - 1 = 2$. Expression simplifies to `*(a + 2)`, which corresponds to element `a[2]`, equal to 3.
Incorrect. 2 is result of intermediate difference calculation $3 - 1$.
Incorrect. 1 is initial element `a[0]`.
Incorrect. Using arithmetic expressions in indexing is strictly permitted.
